MCMC_MULTIMODAL.rationale: 10 well-separated modes with varying variances requires sophisticated MCMC (parallel tempering or replica exchange). Standard Metropolis-Hastings will get stuck in one mode.
The Rosenbrock/banana-shaped posterior has extreme correlation and curvature, causing standard MCMC to have ESS/sample near zero. Requires HMC with tuned mass matrix.
21 modes with Cauchy tails means infinite variance. Posterior mass at infinity is non-negligible. Standard MCMC theory breaks down completely.
500-dimensional space with 12 modes. Curse of dimensionality makes mode-hopping exponentially rare. Requires advanced methods like SMC or variational inference.
Neal's funnel has a scale that varies by exp(3) = 20x across dimensions. Standard HMC diverges in the narrow part. Requires reparameterization or NUTS with adaptation.

HEAVY_TAIL.rationale: Cauchy distribution has no mean or variance. Standard numerical CDF computation fails for extreme quantiles due to catastrophic cancellation.
Pareto with alpha=0.5 has no moments at all. PDF computation at extreme values requires careful handling of underflow. Tail probability P(X > x) = x^(-0.5) decays slowly.
Levy distribution has infinite mean and extremely heavy right tail. Quantile at p=1-1e-10 is astronomically large. Numerical inversion of CDF fails without special handling.
Student-t with df=2.01 has variance = 2.01/(2.01-2) = 201 but no skewness or kurtosis. Sample estimates will be wildly unstable even with 1M samples.
Sum of Cauchy variables is Cauchy - but NOT via central limit theorem (which requires finite variance). Numerical convolution via FFT will fail due to infinite tails.

optimization_rosenbrock.rationale: The Rosenbrock function has a long, narrow, parabolic valley. The global minimum is inside this valley but finding it requires navigating a curved path. Starting from x = [-1, -1, ...] requires the algorithm to first reach the valley mouth and then navigate the entire length. L-BFGS helps with memory but not with the fundamental geometry.
